sentence: Though it may seem extreme, a multilingual can quite literally feel differently about people, events or things when using one language versus another. The likelihood of being rattled by curse words or taboo words changes across native and second languages. Speakers of multiple languages not only report feeling different, but their bodies have different physiological reactions and their minds make different emotionally driven decisions across languages. The exact relationship between positive and negative emotions and language varies across people. For some, the second language carries more positive connotations because it is associated with freedom, opportunity, financial well-being and escape from persecution, whereas the native language is associated with poverty and hardship. For others, the opposite is true — the second language is associated with post-immigration challenges, discrimination and lack of close relationships, whereas the native language is associated with family, friends and parental love. And many are somewhere in between, having a mix of positive and negative experiences associated with each language.

chunks.text: Though it may seem extreme, a multilingual can quite literally feel differently about people, events or things when using one language versus another.
chunks.ko: 극단적으로 들릴지 모르지만, 다중 언어 사용자는 어떤 언어를 쓰느냐에 따라 사람과 사건, 사물에 대해 정말 말 그대로 다르게 느낄 수 있다
chunks.praise: quite literally를 '말 그대로'로 본 거 정말 잘했어요.

chunks.text: The likelihood of being rattled by curse words or taboo words changes across native and second languages.
chunks.ko: 욕설이나 금기어에 흔들릴 가능성은 모국어냐 제2언어냐에 따라 달라진다

points.en: changes across native and second languages

chunks.text: Speakers of multiple languages not only report feeling different, but their bodies have different physiological reactions and their minds make different emotionally driven decisions across languages.
chunks.ko: 여러 언어를 쓰는 사람들은 다르게 느낀다고 말할 뿐 아니라, 몸이 다른 생리적 반응을 보이고 마음도 언어에 따라 감정에 이끌린 다른 결정을 내린다
chunks.praise: not only A but B를 두 갈래로 살린 거 정말 잘했어요.

chunks.text: The exact relationship between positive and negative emotions and language varies across people.
chunks.ko: 긍정적·부정적 감정과 언어 사이의 정확한 관계는 사람마다 다르다
chunks.praise: varies across people을 '사람마다 다르다'로 본 거 좋아요.

chunks.text: For some, the second language carries more positive connotations because it is associated with freedom, opportunity, financial well-being and escape from persecution,
chunks.ko: 어떤 사람에게는 제2언어가 더 긍정적인 느낌을 지닌다. 자유, 기회, 경제적 안정, 박해에서의 탈출과 이어져 있기 때문이다
chunks.praise: carries connotations를 '느낌을 지닌다'로 본 거 정말 잘했어요.

errors.ask: carry가 뜻이나 느낌과 같이 오면 어떻게 될까요?

chunks.text: whereas the native language is associated with poverty and hardship.
chunks.ko: 반면에 모국어는 가난, 고생과 이어져 있다

chunks.text: For others, the opposite is true — the second language is associated with post-immigration challenges, discrimination and lack of close relationships,
chunks.ko: 다른 사람에게는 그 반대다 — 제2언어가 이민 후의 어려움, 차별, 가까운 관계의 부족과 이어져 있다
chunks.praise: the opposite is true를 '그 반대다'로 본 거 정말 잘했어요.

errors.detect: the opposite is true를 '반대가 사실이다'로 어색하게 두고 뜻을 흐림

chunks.text: whereas the native language is associated with family, friends and parental love.
chunks.ko: 반면에 모국어는 가족, 친구, 부모의 사랑과 이어져 있다
chunks.praise: parental love를 '부모의 사랑'으로 본 거 좋아요.

chunks.text: And many are somewhere in between, having a mix of positive and negative experiences associated with each language.
chunks.ko: 그리고 많은 사람은 그 중간 어딘가에 있어서, 각 언어마다 긍정적 경험과 부정적 경험이 섞여 있다
chunks.praise: somewhere in between을 '중간 어딘가'로 본 거 정말 잘했어요.

errors.detect: having을 새 문장의 동사로 보고 끊음
